title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was used to create non-consensual intimate imagery of a real person without her knowledge or permission. The deployer of the system, a 22-year-old man, obtained source photographs from the victim's private social media account and used AI tools to generate explicit morphed images. He then distributed this synthetic content through multiple fake accounts across multiple platforms, accompanied by threatening messages.

This is a case of a technology deployed with no restrictions on its use and no human review of outputs. The victim discovered the abuse only after receiving threatening messages about the fake content. The attacker used throwaway accounts and email addresses specifically to evade accountability. The system itself had no mechanism to prevent its use for creating intimate imagery or to alert the victim to the generated content.

It is not established what AI system was used, whether it was commercially available or custom-built, or what safeguards, if any, it contained before this deployment.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and distributing artificial intelligence-generated obscene images of a college acquaintance. Bansal allegedly obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used AI technology to create explicit morphed images. He then circulated this content through multiple fake Instagram, Discord, and Facebook accounts, using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity and sending threatening messages to the victim.

The case began when the 22-year-old woman reported the harassment to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi after receiving messages about the fake content being shared. Police conducted a detailed digital investigation, analyzing social media accounts and email records to trace the connections between the fake profiles. During interrogation, Bansal admitted he knew the victim from college and harbored personal resentment toward her. Police recovered his mobile phone and other digital evidence, and investigation is ongoing.
